basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Requires one profile: a programme coordinates related components for benefits, a portfolio selects and balances investments.
Holds aggregate scope and membership, while each project or operation keeps its own record.
Separates output, outcome, benefit and causal attribution; spending does not prove benefit.
Covers prioritisation and reallocation decisions that single projects do not have.

may: Aggregate status, cost and risk from component records for reporting.
Map dependencies and alignment to strategy objectives.
Model prioritisation scenarios for decision makers.
mustNot: Admit, remove or reprioritise components without governance approval.
Report a benefit as realized from completion or spend alone.
Change component data in the projects it aggregates.
Hide disbenefits or negative outcomes from reviews.
Create an aggregate root with an ambiguous profile.
requiresHuman: Starting, closing or changing the mandate of a programme or portfolio.

considerations: Portfolio choices allocate public or company resources and affect people who depend on the funded work.
Disbenefits often fall on groups who are not stakeholders in the decision.
Honest benefit reporting matters for accountability of public spending.

items: A programme or portfolio has a mandate, a sponsor, a declared profile, components and a governance body.
It is confused with a large project, an initiative, a strategy or an organisational unit.
Resources locked in failing components because aggregate reporting hides them.
Double counting of benefits across components.
AXELOS Managing Successful Programmes (MSP) and MoP.
